topic.title: Your phone's map of where you go
topic.question: Is my phone keeping a record of where I go, and how do I check?

intent.whoThisHelps: Phone owners who never knew their phone can keep a history of places they visit.
intent.whatTheyLearn: iPhone (Significant Locations & Routes) and Google Maps Timeline can keep a record of places and routes, and where each setting lives.
intent.whatTheyCanDo: Find the setting, look, then keep it or turn it off; on Google Maps, choose an auto-delete period.
intent.whyEvidenceSupportsIt: Apple and Google document these features and their settings on their own pages.
intent.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: It does not show that anyone else reads this data, does not cover other apps that use location, and menu names can differ by version and language.

claims.text: With Significant Locations & Routes on, an iPhone keeps track of places you have recently been, how often and when you visited them, and the routes you take.
claims.limitations: Applies when the setting is on; Apple says the data is used to learn places and routes significant to you.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

claims.text: Apple says Significant Locations & Routes are synced between your devices with end-to-end encryption and cannot be read by Apple.
claims.limitations: Apple's own statement about its encryption; not independently verified.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

claims.text: On iPhone the setting is at Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Significant Locations & Routes, where it can be turned off.
claims.limitations: Menu names can differ by iOS version and language.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

claims.text: When Google Maps Timeline is on, it automatically saves your visits and routes, saving your devices' precise locations to the device, including when Google apps aren't open.
claims.limitations: Applies only when Timeline is turned on; Google says the data is saved to each signed-in device.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

claims.text: On Android, Timeline is in Google Maps: tap your profile picture or initial, then Your Timeline; it can be turned off in Location & privacy settings.
claims.limitations: Menu names can differ by app version and language.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

claims.text: Google Maps Timeline can automatically delete data older than 3, 18 or 36 months; 36 months is three years.
claims.limitations: These are the auto-delete choices Google lists; the page does not say what happens when auto-delete is off.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner; the owner's own documentation is the authoritative source for what its software does.

evidence.supportingPassage: Significant Locations & Routes: Your iPhone and other devices where you sign in to iCloud with your Apple Account will keep track of places you have recently been, how often and when you visited them, and the routes you take to get there, in order to learn places and routes that are significant to you.
Your Significant Locations & Routes are synced between your devices using end-to-end encryption and cannot be read by Apple.
On your iPhone or iPad: Go to Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > then turn off Significant Locations & Routes.
evidence.locator: Section: Turn off Significant Locations & Routes

evidence.supportingPassage: Timeline helps you go back in time and remember where you've been by automatically saving your visits and routes to your Google Maps Timeline on each of your signed-in devices.
When you turn on Timeline, you consent to Google regularly saving each of your devices' precise locations to that device, to show you where you've been, including when Google apps aren't open.
Tap your profile picture or initial Your Timeline .
Under "Location settings," check that it says "Timeline is on
evidence.locator: Section: Turn Timeline on or off

evidence.supportingPassage: You can choose to automatically delete Timeline data that's older than 3 months, 18 months, or 36 months.
